title: Everybody Wants Hera Pheri 3. Nobody Can Agree on Who Owns It.
excerpt: Akshay Kumar's production house just fired a legal warning shot, Priyadarshan says the franchise is 'dead,' and a three-way rights war now holds Bollywood's most beloved comedy hostage.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Hera Pheri 3 is embroiled in a legal dispute among three claimants.
  • Akshay Kumar's production house asserts exclusive rights to the film.
  • Director Priyadarshan has distanced himself from the project, calling it 'dead.'
  • The franchise's ownership conflict threatens its long-awaited third installment.
  • Hera Pheri is a cultural phenomenon with significant global demand.

There is exactly one sequel that every Indian, everywhere in the world, has been waiting for since 2006. Not a superhero tentpole. Not a period epic. A comedy about three broke men, a kidnapping gone wrong, and the most quotable dialogue in Hindi cinema history.

And right now, Hera Pheri 3 is stuck in a legal cage match between three parties who all claim they own it.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=bddede3ymnU

The Opening Salvo

On July 4, Akshay Kumar's production house, Cape of Good Films LLP, published a formal notice in *Complete Cinema* magazine that read like a declaration of war. The company asserted that it holds the "irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual and unencumbered licence" to produce, distribute, market, and commercially exploit Hera Pheri 3 — across all platforms, technologies, and formats, "whether currently known or developed in the future."

The notice didn't name names. It didn't have to. It warned distributors, OTT platforms, cinema chains, broadcasters, and every other stakeholder in the business against cutting a deal with anyone else claiming rights to the film. The message was unmistakable: if you want Hera Pheri 3, you come to us.

The Director Who Walked Away

This legal escalation didn't come out of nowhere. Days earlier, Priyadarshan — the man who directed the original 2000 masterpiece — confirmed he was out. Not quietly. Not diplomatically. With the kind of scorched-earth honesty Bollywood rarely sees.

> "Dhurandhar — Ranveer Singh's record-shattering action franchise — currently sits at over ₹3,100 crore worldwide."

> "Hera Pheri was born, Hera Pheri 2 became sick, and Hera Pheri 3 will be dead." — Priyadarshan

The filmmaker alleged that original franchise producer Firoz Nadiadwala had "insulted" him repeatedly, even telling Akshay Kumar not to make the third film with him. According to Priyadarshan, Nadiadwala dismissed his cut of the original Hera Pheri as a "poor man's version" — a staggering insult for a film that became one of the most rewatched comedies in Indian cinema.

> "If I had directed it, I could've made it bigger than Dhurandhar." — Priyadarshan

That claim isn't idle boasting. Dhurandhar — Ranveer Singh's record-shattering action franchise — currently sits at over ₹3,100 crore worldwide. Priyadarshan was essentially saying: you had a goldmine, and you let ego bury it.

![Akshay Kumar — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2a/Akshay_Kumar_National_Award_for_Padman_%28cropped%29.jpg)

Three Parties, One Franchise, Zero Clarity

The rights tangle goes deeper than a producer-director feud. At least three entities are now claiming ownership:

Cape of Good Films (Akshay Kumar) asserts an exclusive worldwide licence. Their public notice suggests they believe the rights have legally transferred to them.

Firoz Nadiadwala, the man who originally produced both Hera Pheri films, filed an FIR back in April over the franchise rights dispute. He told Bollywood Hungama in late June that the film was happening "very soon."

Ownership Tug-of-War
Cape of Good Films (Akshay Kumar)
Exclusive worldwide license
Firoz Nadiadwala
Filed FIR over rights dispute
Seven Arts Films (GP Vijayakumar)
Claims 100% IP ownership

Seven Arts Films' GP Vijayakumar entered the picture earlier in 2026, claiming "100 percent IP ownership" of the franchise and warning that production without his authorisation would constitute legal infringement. It was Vijayakumar's intervention in 2025 that first spooked Priyadarshan into hesitating.

Three claimants. One franchise. And a beloved cast — Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty, and Paresh Rawal — caught in the crossfire.

Meanwhile, Akshay Moves On (Sort Of)

The irony is rich. While the Hera Pheri 3 saga spirals into legal paralysis, Akshay and Priyadarshan have already confirmed their ninth collaboration together — a comedy-thriller titled Wicked Sunny. The director-star relationship is clearly intact. It's the franchise's ownership structure that's broken.

Akshay, for his part, is having a strong 2026. His Welcome To The Jungle just crossed ₹100 crore domestically in its second weekend, making it his 21st film in the prestigious century club. He doesn't need Hera Pheri 3 to stay relevant. But the franchise needs resolution to stay alive.

What This Means for the Diaspora

If you're reading this from New York, Toronto, or London, you already know: Hera Pheri isn't just a comedy. It's cultural currency. The Babu Bhaiya memes, the "25 din mein paisa double" references, the sheer joy of quoting Raju, Shyam, and Babu Rao at family gatherings — this franchise is woven into every NRI household's DNA.

The demand for a third film has been loud, consistent, and global for nearly two decades. OTT platforms would pay a fortune for the streaming rights alone. International theatrical distributors have been circling the project for years.

Cultural Impact of Hera Pheri
›20 years of demand Hera Pheri is a beloved comedy franchise.
›Widespread meme references Memorable quotes are part of Indian culture.
›High streaming rights value Significant interest from international distributors.

And yet, here we are. Three parties fighting in court. A director who's walked away in disgust. And a trilogy that may never be completed — not because audiences don't want it, but because the people who own it can't stop fighting over it.

Some comedies write themselves. This one, apparently, can't even get past the lawyers.
